outcome: Resolve player issues faster with version-correct, cited answers — and turn consented support and community signals into prioritised, source-linked product insight
overview: Support agents hunt through account, build, entitlement and policy systems while community feedback piles up in channels nobody has time to read, so backlogs grow and emerging issues surface only after they trend publicly. This solution retrieves version-correct answers with citations, performs a narrow set of authorised account actions under permission limits, and clusters consented support and community signals into prioritised, source-linked product themes. Safety reports are handed to trained moderators rather than answered by automation. A 6–10-week pilot targets shorter handling time and better first-contact resolution while entitlement accuracy and safety escalation hold. Reference builds are specified for AWS and Azure, with Arabic and English support delivery.

benefits.text: Reduce average handling time by around 25% with cited, build-version-correct answers
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Validated on the customer’s own contact mix; gains depend on knowledge-base coverage and how well build versions are tracked

benefits.text: Improve first-contact resolution and reduce repeat contacts on the same issue
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on the account actions the customer authorises; issues needing engineering fixes cannot be resolved at first contact whatever the tooling

benefits.text: Detect emerging issues earlier by clustering consented support and community signals with source links
benefits.source: Reference design capability, Redington Gaming catalogue
benefits.limits: Community sentiment reflects the players who post, not the player base; themes are prioritisation prompts for humans, never a representative population measure

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); player contacts, account data and consented community extracts remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No maintained knowledge base or build-version records
notFor.why: Answers must be traceable to a policy or patch note for a specific build; without versioned sources the assistant confidently cites content that no longer applies

notFor.situation: No account-action permission model or audit trail
notFor.why: Entitlement grants, restores and compensation need scoped permissions and logging; without them, automation risks over-compensation and disclosure

notFor.situation: Community data with no consent basis or platform terms permitting analysis
notFor.why: Analysing player conversations without a lawful basis and platform permission is surveillance, not insight

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns answer policy, compensation limits, community consent basis and all moderation decisions · Duration: 6–10-week pilot; further 12–22 weeks to full support scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, conversational-AI engineer, support operations consultant; customer player-support owner, community manager, knowledge owner, privacy reviewer, trust-and-safety contact · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and support baseline agreement
2) Knowledge, build-version and CRM integration
3) Permission model, action limits and audit configuration
4) Community source onboarding and theme-model tuning
5) Agent-assist pilot with weekly quality and safety review
6) Stabilisation and handover
